title: Associations between gestational exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances, fetal growth, and the mediation effect of thyroid hormones.
ehr_evidence: Study participants were selected among subjects of the Ezhou birth cohort study, which is an ongoing longitudinal study initiated in January 2019 that aims to evaluate the impact of environmental factors on the health of pregnant women and their children.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating associations between prenatal PFAS exposure, maternal thyroid hormones, and fetal growth outcomes in China.
key_findings: Increasing PFNA concentration was associated with decreased birth length (β = -0.54 cm; 95% CI: -0.90, -0.18).
Increasing PFHxS concentration was associated with decreased birth length (β = -0.64 cm; 95% CI: -0.86, -0.42).
Increasing PFOA concentration was associated with decreased head circumference (β = -0.73 cm; 95% CI: -1.19, -0.27).
Increasing PFHpS concentration was associated with decreased head circumference (β = -0.30 cm; 95% CI: -0.53, -0.07).
Increasing PFDA concentration was associated with decreased gestational age (β = -0.18 week; 95% CI: -0.26, -0.10).
Maternal FT3 mediated 36.7% of the effect of PFNA on birth length, and FT4 mediated 30.8% of the effect of PFOA on head circumference.
No significant mediation by thyroid hormones was observed for birth weight or gestational age.
In female infants, higher PFOA was associated with lower birth weight (β = -53.6 g; 95% CI: -77.8, -29.4).
captured_features: maternal thyroid hormone levels (TSH, FT3, FT4, TT3, TT4, TG)
study_design: prospective birth cohort study with mediation analysis
population: 379 mother-infant pairs from Ezhou City, Hubei Province, China, recruited in early pregnancy (2019-2020)
limitations: PFAS-thyroid hormone associations are cross-sectional, limiting causal inference
single first-trimester measurement may lead to exposure misclassification
only 8 of over 23 detectable PFASs were measured
single-city cohort limits generalizability to other populations
data_availability_statement: The datasets used and/or analysed during the current study available from the corresponding author on reason-able request.
